html:
Charles V was the Habsburg ruler who inherited more of Europe and the Americas than anyone before him: king of Spain from 1516 and Holy Roman Emperor from 1519, until he gave up his crowns in 1555 and 1556. He was born in Ghent in 1500.

From his four grandparents he received:

  • the Burgundian Netherlands, which he joined into the Seventeen Provinces of the Habsburg Netherlands;
  • Castile and Aragon, with their Italian lands and the new empire in the Americas;
  • the Habsburg lands in Austria, and the chance to be elected emperor of the Holy Roman Empire, which he won with loans from Jakob Fugger.

In his reign Cortés and Pizarro conquered the Aztec and Inca empires, and the fleet of Magellan sailed round the world under his flag. His New Laws of 1542 tried to curb the abuse of Native Americans.

In Europe he fought France over Italy for decades and took Milan in 1535; his unpaid troops sacked Rome in 1527. At Worms in 1521 he faced Martin Luther and declared him an outlaw, but he could not stop the Reformation, and pressed the pope to call the Council of Trent. Worn out, he split his realms: Spain, the Netherlands and Italy to his son Philip II, Austria and the empire to his brother Ferdinand. He died in a Spanish monastery in 1558.
sum: Charles V was the Habsburg ruler who inherited more of Europe and the Americas than anyone before him: king of Spain from 1516 and Holy Roman Emperor from 1519, until he gave up his crowns in 1555 and 1556. He was born in Ghent in 1500.
